notes: ADAPTATION: the playable world is a finite streaming window (80 m chunks, radius 2) plus a far skyline LOD (240 m chunks, radius 3) built from the same deterministic building plans. Night is our choice: the page states no time of day; night makes the sourced working lighting (open buildings, the level's own electricity) and the black-mirror sealed buildings legible. Districts follow the page's gradual density change (suburban lots resembling Level 9 in the west, skyscraper blocks in the east, noise in between); street layout, facades and room plans are ours. Street lights and traffic signals work (the level generates its own electricity); signals cycle for no traffic. Open ground floors are public rooms (shops, laundromats, offices, lobbies) with sparse furnishing; upper floors and suburban houses are not enterable in this slice. Sealed buildings (one third, per page) have black-mirror windows and locked doors. Fluidity (cars between kerb and car park, ads changing or fading, roadworks appearing) only happens to things outside the camera view. Canal: one sourced canal following a road line, with bridges, swimmable water and wall ladders. The exit street near spawn (barricade, memorial, painted safe-route trail, arcade machine in the road, arcade building, out-of-place elevator, recruitment poster) is authored; farther out, arcade buildings, street elevators and arcade machines in plazas/parks recur procedurally. The memorial is generic (no names); the supply note paraphrases the Malt Marters practice. Arrivals: from_L009 on a western suburban street (page: arrivals in suburban lots mistake it for Level 9); from_L025 beside the arcade machine in the road. Not built: the ~40 other documented exits (they remain documented in transitions.json), communities (Capital, New Times Square, Base Beta and others: their locations are not given), subways and trains.
